summary: Newtown has seen rising crime since September 2023, including increases in assaults, burglaries, vandalism, juvenile delinquency, drug offences and cybercrime. The note describes a multi-sector response: a citizen-led Newtown Action Committee, academic analysis, school intervention programs, predictive policing, community policing, a cybersecurity task force and a business security program. It concludes that residents are taking decisive action to restore safety.
one_line: Newtown responds to a crime surge since September 2023 with citizen action, data analysis, schools, policing, technology and business initiatives.
key_facts: Crime in Newtown has been rising since September 2023, according to the Newtown Police Department report published November 15, 2023: assaults up 15%, burglaries up 22%, vandalism up 30%.
Jonathan Harrow, a lifelong resident, founded the Newtown Action Committee (NAC) on October 3, 2023, a grassroots group addressing root causes of crime.
The NAC partnered with criminologist Dr. Susan Clarke; a study released December 1, 2023 found thefts were 66% more frequent on poorly lit streets than in well-lit areas.
The Newtown Economic Research Initiative (NERI) found unemployment rose to 7.5% in the last quarter, up from 5.4% the year prior; director Michael Zheng linked economic despair to crime.
The NAC found a 20% rise in juvenile delinquency since September 2023; schools launched early intervention programs, led by Principal Angela Roberts of Newtown High, launched January 10, 2024.
The Newtown precinct received a federal grant on October 20, 2023 to buy software that predicts crime hotspots and optimizes patrol routes.
Drug-related offences peaked at a 40% increase; narcotics officer Javier Dominguez leads operations to dismantle local drug supply chains, as stated at a February 8, 2024 press conference.
Sergeant Rebecca Lee drives the community policing initiative to build trust between police and residents, speaking at an outreach event on February 20, 2024.
The Newtown Cybersecurity Task Force, headed by tech entrepreneur Amir Patel, formed in January 2024 to address a 25% increase in cybercrimes.
Newtown Chamber of Commerce President Emma Thompson started the 'Safe Shopper' program on December 22, 2023 to help businesses upgrade surveillance and train staff in security awareness.
Chief of Police Alicia Gutierrez said of the crime surge: 'We are facing an uphill battle. But we are not backing down.'
